text: This is what in-house counsel actually sends back to a vendor: tracked changes and comments in Word. Producing it takes one to three hours per contract.

Every company has a playbook — preferred, fallback, and walk-away positions. The bottleneck is applying it, clause by clause, across twenty to sixty pages, without missing the term hidden in a definition three sections away.

The naive approach is to paste the contract into a chat assistant. Here is our fair baseline: the same model, the same playbook, and one prompt. It finds {{B1_F1}} of the issues, cites sections that do not exist {{B1_HALL}} of the time, and cannot touch the document.
Playbook Redliner starts with the vendor's actual Word file and the company's versioned review playbook.
For this run, we will use a realistic hosting agreement from the evaluation set, with lawyer-confirmed gold labels.
The document becomes a clause-addressable model. The planner maps each of eighteen rules to the sections and definitions that matter, then starts one drafter per rule.

Each worker can read sections, search the contract, resolve definitions, and validate every edit anchor. Findings arrive as soon as they are independently verified, so counsel can start reviewing before the run finishes.
Nothing is written until I decide. I move with J and K, then accept, edit, or reject. Here I change the liability cap before accepting it, and reject a different proposal.
The liability language started from a precedent the team approved last month. Accepted wording becomes memory for the next contract.
Export writes a new copy: real Word tracked changes, real margin comments, author Playbook Redliner, and nothing else touched.
The assembler also produces an issues memo, ordered by what counsel should resolve before signature.

The hard case is a cap that says twelve months' Fees, while Fees is defined elsewhere as a one-off implementation fee. The baseline calls it compliant. The drafter resolved the definition, and the trajectory shows every tool call.

On twelve contracts — eight real, lawyer-labelled SEC filings and four seeded synthetic ones — detection F one went from {{B1_F1}} to {{FINAL_F1}}, redline validity from {{B1_VALID}} to {{FINAL_VALID}}, and hallucinated citations from {{B1_HALL}} to {{FINAL_HALL}}.
The biggest single gain came from {{BIGGEST}}. We also removed the monolith — one agent for all eighteen rules — because {{X_REASON}}. Every step stays in the measured changelog.
{{HOT_TAKE_LINE}} The real product is not an answer. It is a reviewable artifact with evidence.
Playbook Redliner. Everything reproduces from the repository with one command.
